name: The Pool Room
summary: Step inside a New York dive-bar film and watch the final pool break.
tagline: A made-up bar. A real pool break.
lead: Step inside an original 3D bar, then watch the final pool shot play out inside the room.
tileDescription: Step inside. Watch the cue ball fly.

sections.heading: Built from scratch
paragraphs: The room, props, lighting, and shots were created for this original showroom build. It is not a real bar or a client space.
The scene is designed to show how a concept can feel tangible before a physical location or shoot exists.

sections.heading: A room with a point of view
paragraphs: The visual system uses a dive-bar setting to make material, light, sound, and motion part of one authored moment.
It is a Lab experiment, not evidence of client work or a real-world outcome.

disclaimer: An original Little Fight Lab concept.
interactionNotes: Watch the cinematic opening and pool-break film.
tileImageAlt: The imagined Pool Room bar, with neon in the window and a green pool table.

name: Six-Story Walk-Up
summary: Spin around a made-up New York corner and see every angle.
lead: Drag around an invented walk-up, tilt up to the roof, and zoom into the details.
tileDescription: Spin a tiny New York corner.

sections.heading: Explore the whole corner
paragraphs: The walkthrough uses a single interactive 3D environment rather than a fixed image.
It is an illustrative capability build for thinking about place, not a client result.

disclaimer: An illustrative Little Fight Lab concept.
interactionNotes: Drag sideways to orbit, drag vertically to tilt, and pinch or scroll to zoom.
tileImageAlt: Warm windows, brickwork, and fire escapes on the interactive New York walk-up.

name: Neon District
summary: Tap into a neon city of cabs, citizens, beacons, and changing weather.
tagline: The city changes when you touch it.
lead: Spin through an invented district, tap a beacon, then switch the scene from lunch rush to rain or night.
tileDescription: Make it rain on a neon city.

sections.heading: A city you can touch
paragraphs: Beacons, citizens, and cabs invite interaction while a guided tour moves through the scene.
Time-of-day and event controls change the illustrative environment without making a business-performance claim.

disclaimer: An illustrative Little Fight Lab concept.
interactionNotes: Tap beacons, citizens, and cabs; drag to orbit; pinch to zoom; use the on-page tour and time controls.
tileImageAlt: The lit streets and yellow windows of Neon District beneath a vivid blue and violet sky.

name: Scroll Into Motion
summary: Use your thumb to cut a 16-frame New York film.
lead: Scroll forward, pull back, or stop on any of sixteen New York frames. The film waits for you.
tileDescription: Slide through sixteen New York scenes.

sections.heading: Scroll is the editor
paragraphs: The study is built around direct control instead of autoplay: the scene changes only when the visitor moves it.
It demonstrates a motion approach for launch films, lookbooks, campaigns, and brand stories.

disclaimer: A Little Fight Lab motion study.
interactionNotes: Scroll forward, pull back, or pause at any moment; the sequence does not autoplay.
tileImageAlt: A crowd moving through Grand Central, one of the New York scenes in the scroll-controlled film.

name: Micro-Animations
summary: Play through seven tiny moments that make software feel alive.
lead: Press, throw, hold, undo, slide, flip, and commit. Every move answers back.
tileDescription: Press, swipe, and flip a tiny app.

sections.heading: Feedback carries the action
paragraphs: The studies focus on button acknowledgement, sheets, destructive holds, undo, tabs, theme changes, and form completion.
The ordering interface is illustrative; it is a place to test motion behavior, not a real order flow or client result.

disclaimer: A Little Fight Lab interaction study.
interactionNotes: Try the press, throw, hold, undo, slide, flip, and commit interactions.
tileImageAlt: The Bodega demo with a coffee added and its sliding shopping bag open.

name: AHA Laser Poster
summary: Pull a chain and watch a wordmark turn into light.
lead: A laser draws the letters. The pull chain changes the room.
tileDescription: Pull the chain. Light up the poster.

sections.heading: Poster as interaction
paragraphs: This is a responsive design demo centered on a laser-drawn wordmark and one pull-chain gesture.
Its AHA name is separate from the After Hours Agenda client/product case study; it is a Lab poster experiment.

disclaimer: A Little Fight Lab poster study.
interactionNotes: Use the pull-chain control to trigger the poster behavior.
tileImageAlt: The AHA poster glowing pink, with its pull chain at the upper right.

name: Studio Engine
summary: Name a business and watch a sample site change shape.
tagline: Type a business. Change the mood.
lead: Choose a sample business, switch the visual direction, and watch the site respond.
tileDescription: Pick a shop. Give it a new look.

sections.heading: Start with a direction
paragraphs: The project uses sample business types and visual directions to demonstrate an interactive starting point.
It is not a real client site or client result.

disclaimer: An illustrative Little Fight Lab tool.
interactionNotes: Select a sample business type and visual direction to drive the illustrative experience.
tileImageAlt: The bright bakery website sketch made in Studio Engine, with bold type and a warm orange illustration.

name: Growth Street
summary: Follow a made-up flower shop from a quiet street to a busy window.
tagline: A flower-shop story told in pictures.
lead: Scroll through an invented shop story that turns discovery, orders, and follow-through into a street scene.
tileDescription: Meet a florist. Follow her shop’s story.

sections.heading: A model for explanation
paragraphs: The flower-shop narrative is invented to show relationships among discovery, action, and follow-through.
Dots, tickets, crowd scenes, reviews, and money are explanatory props, not reported traffic, sales, reviews, or revenue.

disclaimer: An illustrative Little Fight Lab systems story.
interactionNotes: Use the interactive story props to explore the relationship between discovery, action, and follow-through.
tileImageAlt: Rosie’s illustrated flower shop beside a phone, with a striped awning, flowers, and a bright blue sky.

name: Goliath
summary: Scroll through ten Little Fight posters as they paste themselves up.
lead: Scroll forward to paste up the campaign. Pull back to peel it away, frame by frame.
tileDescription: Paste up ten posters with one scroll.

sections.heading: One message, many frames
paragraphs: This is Little Fight’s own campaign study, built around a sequence of ten posters and a scroll-controlled projection effect.
It demonstrates how a clear idea can organize a campaign; it is not a client result.

disclaimer: A Little Fight Lab campaign study.
interactionNotes: Use scroll as the projector that carries the poster sequence.
tileImageAlt: The bold orange Little Fight poster from the scrolling campaign.

name: Cabinet Lab
summary: Try cabinet styles, finishes and hardware before choosing a direction.
tagline: Try the room before choosing a direction.
lead: Compare finishes, cabinet styles, hardware, and lighting in a hands-on visual study.

sections.heading: Start with a direction
paragraphs: Move through a small set of cabinet styles, finishes, and hardware to see how the choices work together.
This is a visual study for early conversations. It is not a quote, construction drawing, order form, or measured plan.

disclaimer: A Little Fight visual study. Not a quote or construction drawing.
interactionNotes: Choose a cabinet style, finish, and viewpoint; save a design to compare it with another.
tileImageAlt: A cabinet design study with a warm wood island, painted cabinetry, and adjustable room controls.

name: Property Explorer
summary: Explore a fictional property, reveal its structure, and find the systems behind the walls.
tagline: Understand a place, inside and out.
lead: Move around a fictional property, reveal the frame, and locate example plumbing, electrical, and air systems.

sections.heading: Explore. Reveal. Find.
paragraphs: Start with the finished exterior, then reveal the framing or search for a system behind the walls.
The property, floor plan, dimensions, and service routes were created for this demonstration. They are not a client location or construction record.
bullets: Finished property with day and evening light
Exposed framing and a section view
Searchable systems and a demonstration plan

disclaimer: Fictional property and illustrative systems. Not a construction drawing or client location.
interactionNotes: Drag to orbit or use the view controls. Open Inside to reveal the frame, or Find a system to inspect a component.
tileImageAlt: Fictional property model with a pitched-roof house, landscaping, and a connected driveway.
